title: A vendor's core charge on the bill posts as cost with the bill line
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure the General Internal category is mapped to an expense account, account X, at the test location.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Approved, with one special-order part with a core, received, no bill yet.
custom_steps:
1. Enter the vendor bill for work order 1's special-order part at $125.00 with a core charge of $30.00.
  2. In QuickBooks Online, open that vendor bill.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The bill is saved.

Step 2:

  • The part line and the $30.00 core charge both post to account X.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-R3: “When a vendor bill is created for a special-order part or a sublet on a work order that is already internal or no charge, the bill line posts to the mapped expense account instead of Cost of Parts (or the category account); the vendor, the bill and Accounts Payable are unchanged. This covers the bill of a vendor-bought job entered as a special-order part (sublet, Terminology) and the vendor's core charge (S2-E7).”
  • S2-E7: “Parts with a core charge work as today up to resolution: the core row shows on the lines with no price, Core OK / Not OK is required before Close as it is before invoicing, and the completion wizard shows no core amount on an internal or no-charge work order. Not OK adds a charge to nobody; the vendor's core charge on the bill is cost and posts with the bill line (S7-R3). OK creates the vendor return as today, and its credit posts as in S7-R3a. Core cost is never part of Parts cost on the document or in the report. A stock part picked with its core posts both costs at Close, so the Close confirmation row says what posts: "Stock parts $[amount], includes $[core amount] core cost · Posted to [account]"; the document and the report keep Parts cost without cores.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
